title: The edit that changed nothing
brief:
**PAGE 09:04 · shop.example.com · P3**

The 09:00 maintenance window started, but customers still see the normal shop page and can reach checkout. Sam edited `/etc/nginx/sites-available/shop` (new banner page and a `/healthz` endpoint), ran `nginx -t` and reloaded. No errors, no change.

The runbook then says to run `sudo shopctl status`. It prints an HTTP code nobody recognises, and `shopctl version` says `1.0`, although the vendor package installed 2.3.1 last week.

This box is `lab`; you have sudo. Find out which files the system **really** uses, and make the edited ones the live ones. Don't delete the vendor install.

tasks.title: Which file does nginx really load?
tasks.text:
nginx only reads what `nginx.conf` includes. Find the file that defines `shop.example.com` in the **loaded** configuration and compare it with the one Sam edited. `ls -l`, `stat` and `nginx -T` are your friends.

Fix it the Debian/Ubuntu way, so that the next edit of `sites-available/shop` takes effect after a reload. Test the config before you reload. Done when `curl http://127.0.0.1/` shows the maintenance banner, `/healthz` answers 200, and nginx still starts at boot.
hints: `ls -l /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/` shows an arrow (`->`) for a link. No arrow means a separate file that nobody edits any more.
Remove the stale copy, then `sudo ln -s /etc/nginx/sites-available/shop /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/shop`, `sudo nginx -t` and `sudo systemctl reload nginx`.

questions.prompt: What file type does `stat -c %F /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/shop` print before your fix?
From which directory does Ubuntu's nginx.conf include site files (besides conf.d)?

checks.describe: sites-enabled/shop links to sites-available/shop, nginx serves the banner and /healthz, and starts at boot

tasks.title: Which shopctl runs?
tasks.text:
When you type a command, the shell searches the directories in `$PATH` from left to right and runs the **first** match. `sudo` uses its own `secure_path`. Find every `shopctl` the shell can see and where the vendor's 2.3.1 lives (its README is under `/opt/shop/share`).

Make `shopctl` mean the vendor binary for every user and for sudo, without copying it, so the next package upgrade is picked up automatically. Done when `shopctl version` prints `shopctl 2.3.1` everywhere.
hints: `type -a shopctl` lists every match in PATH order; `echo $PATH` and `sudo grep -r secure_path /etc/sudoers /etc/sudoers.d` show the search lists.
Remove the hand-copied file in `/usr/local/sbin`, then link the vendor binary into a standard directory: `sudo ln -s /opt/shop/bin/shopctl /usr/local/bin/shopctl`. Run `hash -r` in an open shell.

questions.prompt: Which bash builtin and option list every `shopctl` the shell can find, in PATH order?
In which directory was the stale `shopctl` 1.0?

checks.describe: every shopctl on the user and sudo PATH resolves to /opt/shop/bin/shopctl (2.3.1)

walkthrough:
### What was broken
1. `/etc/nginx/sites-enabled/shop` was a **regular file**, a copy made months ago with `cp`, not a symlink. nginx includes `sites-enabled/*`, so it kept loading the copy and never saw Sam's edit in `sites-available/shop`.
2. An old `shopctl` 1.0 sat in `/usr/local/sbin`, which comes **before** `/usr/bin` in PATH. The vendor's 2.3.1 lives in `/opt/shop/bin`, which is on nobody's PATH.

### Task 1: the config that is really loaded
```bash
nginx -T | grep -n '^# configuration file'   # every file nginx loaded, in order
ls -l /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/              # no "->" arrow: a copy, not a link
stat -c %F /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/shop     # "regular file"
diff /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/shop /etc/nginx/sites-available/shop
```
*Why:* `nginx -T` prints the effective config with the file each block came from, so you stop guessing which file matters.
```bash
sudo rm /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/shop
sudo ln -s /etc/nginx/sites-available/shop /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/shop
sudo nginx -t && sudo systemctl reload nginx
curl -s http://127.0.0.1/ | grep MAINTENANCE ; curl -i http://127.0.0.1/healthz
```
*Why:* on Debian/Ubuntu, `sites-available` holds every site, and `sites-enabled` holds **links** to the enabled ones. A link means there is exactly one file to edit.

### Task 2: which binary runs
```bash
type -a shopctl          # /usr/local/sbin/shopctl first: the 1.0 copy
echo "$PATH" ; sudo grep -r secure_path /etc/sudoers   # user PATH and sudo's secure_path
cat /opt/shop/share/README
sudo rm /usr/local/sbin/shopctl
sudo ln -s /opt/shop/bin/shopctl /usr/local/bin/shopctl
hash -r ; shopctl version ; sudo shopctl status
```
*Why:* `/usr/local/bin` is the FHS place for locally added admin tools and is on every PATH, including sudo's `secure_path`. A link (not a copy) follows the vendor's upgrades. `hash -r` clears bash's remembered command locations.

### Lessons
- When a change "does nothing", first prove which file the program loads (`nginx -T`, `apachectl -S`, `systemctl cat`).
- Prefer links to copies for config and binaries; copies drift silently.

**Source (adapted):** [sites-enabled and sites-available confusion](https://www.akamai.com/cloud/community/questions/6592/sites-enabled-and-sites-available-confusion): a real file in `sites-enabled` instead of a link. The fix was to move it to `sites-available` and enable it with a link.
